title: Taming the AI Hardware Cambrian Explosion — Abdul Dakkak, Modular
talk_summary: This is a vendor pitch for Modular's Mojo/Max/Modular Cloud stack, arguing that a unified hardware-abstraction layer lets you run models faster and cheaper across heterogeneous accelerators. The content is almost entirely about GPU kernel performance and inference serving, not about agent orchestration, review, or work management.

takeaways.technique: Hardware-agnostic serving layer to unlock cheaper accelerators
takeaways.what_they_do: They abstract hardware behind one stack so the same model can run on Nvidia, AMD, or other accelerators, letting you pick the cheapest capable hardware per workload.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can actually use different hardware. You're not beholden to one hardware provider.
takeaways.numbers: claims 1.5x throughput per GPU vs vLLM on B200; AMD ~30% cheaper than Nvidia equivalent

takeaways.what_they_do: Max APIs let you place prefill on one device and decode on another, matching each phase to the cheapest suitable hardware.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there's nothing to stop you from saying the prefill is on hardware X and the decode is on hardware Y.
